This throwaway page de-risks the in-browser runtime: can `quarto-live`
(Pyodide + micropip) install the climt pure wheel from a URL, import it, and
render a matplotlib figure?

During local spiking the wheel is served from a CORS-enabled localhost server
(`http://127.0.0.1:8912/climt-0.20.0-py3-none-any.whl`). In production this URL
becomes the GitHub release asset
(`https://github.com/CliMT/climt/releases/download/web-demo-v0.20.0/climt-0.20.0-py3-none-any.whl`).

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: true
import micropip
await micropip.install("http://127.0.0.1:8912/climt-0.20.0-py3-none-any.whl")
import climt
print("climt", climt.__version__, "has_fortran:", climt.has_fortran_extensions())
```

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: true
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
x = np.linspace(0, 1, 50)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(x, np.sqrt(x))
ax.set_title("matplotlib in Pyodide")
ax.set_xlabel("x"); ax.set_ylabel("sqrt(x)")
plt.show()
```
